Underrated life advice: Keep proof that good things happen to you. Old photos. Kind messages. Positive feedback. Notes from great days. Whatever. Store them in a single place. Call it a Rainy Day Folder. Pop it open on a bad day and watch your mood turn. It's a free reset button.

There’s nothing more frustrating than realizing where you’d be today if you’d just stopped overthinking and taken action. Don’t let your future self feel that frustration. That thing you want to do? Go do it.

Simple thing that improved my life: I often choose the slower option on purpose. Walk instead of driving. Stairs instead of escalator. Cook instead of ordering. Whatever. In a world that wants you to rush, the ultimate act of rebellion is slowing down. There’s a power in that.

The older I get, the more I realize you can get pretty damn far in life by just doing what most people avoid. Wake up early. Focus deeply. Move your body. Eat real foods. Obsess over one thing. Have difficult conversations. Slow down. Be present. It’s the recipe for a good life.

I’m convinced that your energy creates your reality. Give your energy to stress, complaints, and negative people, they will grow. Give your energy to ambitions, gratitude, and positive people, they will grow. Your energy becomes your destiny. Choose wisely.
